spec_match.rationale: Measures the exact contract — rendering-iteration placement of transitionrun relative to its trigger — using rAF frame counting installed at the moment of the style change, per the HTML event-loop steps.

interactive.rationale: Measure and Clear buttons work; repetitions input respected; the table filled with real medians for all five triggers when exercised.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises counting frames from five trigger points and that is what runs.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles the no-transition timeout branch, suppresses reset transitions explicitly, and documents measurement noise with a repetitions control.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus and event-loop spec links present.

conformance.rationale: The suite asserts the real timing contracts; its two same-iteration assertions honestly FAIL on this build (4 pass / 2 fail), which is the suite doing its job, not a defect in the page.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Measured live on this build: microtask=0, rAF=0, scroll=1, media-query=1, task=1 frames (medians of 5) — the page displayed and explained the late triggers honestly; console clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: triggers-measured fires with condition true, so it can never flag a run where the measurement machinery broke (e.g. all triggers timing out).

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, late/on-time colours on light backgrounds, number input 44px.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled number input, aria-live output, visible focus on tab stops; iframe has a title.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px overflow at 360px; the results table scrolls in its wrapper.

openQuestions.title: Re-measure dispatch timing on stable Chrome 153 — this 153 build still defers mq/scroll transitions
openQuestions.detail: On Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (headless), the media-query and scroll triggers still measure 1 rendering iteration late and the feature conformance suite fails its two same-iteration assertions (4/6). Either the fix landed later in the 153 cycle than this build, it is headless-affected, or it did not ship as listed. Measure on a stable 153 desktop build and update the feature-level notes; this also answers the existing feature-level major question. The setTimeout trigger also measured 1 frame (median of 5) against the page's prediction of 0 — worth re-checking on a non-headless build at the same time.

openQuestions.title: Make triggers-measured falsifiable
openQuestions.detail: Assert at least that no trigger timed out (results.every(r => !r.timedOut)) instead of the literal true, so production telemetry can catch the measurement machinery breaking.

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 full-page screenshots captured and inspected. The measurement design is sound and honest: on this 153 build it correctly reports the OLD (deferred) behaviour for media-query and scroll triggers, matching the conformance suite's 2 failing assertions. The headline work item is re-measuring on stable 153 to establish whether the fix actually shipped.
